# CodeCraft

> An MCP server that checks whether Minecraft Bedrock content will actually
> load. You bring the model — it runs in your own Claude client, on your own
> subscription. CodeCraft never sits in between and never generates content.
> Nine tools, all read-only. The server is stateless and stores nothing.

Endpoint: https://codecraft-ashy-seven.vercel.app/mcp
Source: https://github.com/TanerTalas/codecraft (Apache-2.0)

## Why it exists

Bedrock fails silently. A general model invents a `format_version`, references
a `minecraft:` identifier that does not exist, or calls an API that is not in
`@minecraft/server` — and none of it raises an error until the pack is loaded
in the game. Values are read from version-pinned data, not recalled.

## The nine tools

- check_feasibility — can Bedrock do this at all; if not, why, and what the
  alternative is. Call it first, before any file is written. Input is
  language-independent, output is always English.
- get_version_info — which version number goes where.
- get_schema — which fields this document type requires, and which
  format_version is valid. Returns a summary, not the raw schema.
- lookup_id — does this minecraft: identifier exist in this version, what type
  is it, what block states does it have.
- validate_json — does this file match the official schema. Errors carry a JSON
  pointer, the violated rule, and readable text.
- validate_command — is this command line valid, does it require cheats.
- validate_script — does the script compile with real tsc and real
  @minecraft/server types.
- validate_python — is this out-of-game automation script and the commands
  inside it valid. The hosted endpoint has no Python interpreter, so the syntax
  axis is skipped and reported as syntaxChecked: false.
- review_pack — the whole pack, plus the checks a schema structurally cannot
  see. Call it last.

Call order: check_feasibility, then get_version_info and get_schema, then
review_pack once the files are written.

## Five separate version numbers

- Marketing number, e.g. 26.40 — announcements only, never written to a file.
- Game / data version, e.g. 1.26.40.5 — data indexes.
- min_engine_version, e.g. [1, 26, 40] — manifest.json, three-part array.
- @minecraft/server module version, e.g. 2.9.0 — manifest.json dependencies.
- format_version, e.g. 1.21.100 / 1.13.0 / 2 — content files.

format_version is NOT the game version. It is that document type's own schema
version: block 1.21.100, feature rule 1.13.0, spawn rule 1.8.0, manifest 2.
The module version is 2.x while the game version is 1.26.x; on a prerelease tag
the game version arrives embedded inside the module version, as in
2.11.0-beta.1.26.50-preview.27.

## What it does not catch

- Valid but not intended. The file is correct, the behaviour is wrong.
- Context. A Molang query that exists but is used in the wrong context.
- Silent failure. An entity pointing at a missing loot table loads and drops
  nothing, and the game writes nothing.
- Untried document types. The pack verified in-game touched 11 of 60 types.
